recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current specification already implements the final Jira decision; changing Location.position cardinality or duplicating extension details in core would contradict or over-apply the resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-19725 asked whether Location.position should become an array to represent irregularly shaped locations. The Published / Not Persuasive with Modification resolution kept Location.position as the point/centroid and instead directed implementers to the location-boundary-geojson extension, requested examples using application/geo+json, and requested the VhDir contains search parameter in core for R5.
initial_application: Commit 1eb8e7072a5c7457d14017061f9a1dfac3fc7a81 explicitly applied FHIR-19725 by adding the Location.position comment, Location boundary-search notes, the Washington DC boundary example, the example-list entry, and the imported contains search parameter. Later source changes updated extension links and moved core extensions out to the Extension Pack without changing the applied Location behavior.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has an active location=Location resource entry, so source/location files are in current build scope. The location-boundary-geojson extension now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack under the same canonical URL with Location context, Attachment value, and GeoJSON MIME-type guidance. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant discussion that conflicts with the Jira and git-history conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/location/structuredefinition-Location.xml directs boundary shapes to the standard location-boundary-geojson extension and contains search; source/location/location-notes.xml documents contains; source/location/location-wash-dc-metro.xml uses contentType application/geo+json; and source/location/bundle-Location-search-params.xml defines the contains SearchParameter over the boundary extension value.
